:::{#exm-conditional-mutual-information-nonnegative}
#### Learning a third variable can create information
<!-- no-figure: the example reports a handful of numbers, with nothing to plot -->

Let $X$ and $Y$ be independent fair coins, coded $0$ or $1$,
and let $Z = X + Y \bmod 2$ record whether they differ.
The variables $X$ and $Y$ are independent, so $I(X; Y) = 0$.
Given $Z$, each of $X$ and $Y$ determines the other.
The chunk computes the conditional mutual information from the joint mass function, in [bits](#def-bit).

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
entropy <- function(p) -sum(p[p > 0] * log2(p[p > 0]))
joint <- array(data = 0, dim = c(2, 2, 2))
for (x in 0:1) {
  for (y in 0:1) {
    z <- (x + y) %% 2
    joint[x + 1, y + 1, z + 1] <- 0.25
  }
}
h_xyz <- entropy(joint)
h_xz <- entropy(apply(X = joint, MARGIN = c(1, 3), FUN = sum))
h_yz <- entropy(apply(X = joint, MARGIN = c(2, 3), FUN = sum))
h_z <- entropy(apply(X = joint, MARGIN = 3, FUN = sum))
h_y_given_z <- h_yz - h_z
h_y_given_xz <- h_xyz - h_xz
h_y_given_z - h_y_given_xz
```

So $I(X; Y \mid Z) = `r h_y_given_z - h_y_given_xz`$ bit,
which is nonnegative (@thm-conditional-mutual-information-nonnegative)
even though $I(X; Y) = 0$.

:::
